blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Climate Change Commission (CCC) on Tuesday advised schools and government agencies to shift their schedules ahead of the expected impacts of El Niño in the country. In an interview with Bagong Pilipinas Ngayon, Commissioner Albert dela Cruz suggested that schools adjust their schedules as part of local governments’ implementation of their climate action plans, possibly holding classes from 6 a.m. to 9:30 a.m. “The hours from 10 a.m. to 3 p.m. should be avoided, so if possible, our students should attend classes from 6 a.m. to 9:30 a.m. and then go home,” he said.
